title: Tenant Burst Credit Adjudication Workflow and Operator Playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
summary: This document defines a reproducible, low-latency workflow for adjudicating tenant burst credit usage, reconciling operator actions, and issuing credit adjustments. It covers detection, manual review triage, automated adjudication rules, dashboard signals, incident escalation, and suggested SQL/CLI snippets for operators.
body:
Overview

Purpose: Provide platform operators and SREs with a single reference for handling tenant burst credit disputes and reconciliation requests. The goal is to standardize decisions so that operator interventions are auditable, consistent, and fast.

Scope: Applies to Redwood Dedicated and Hosted customers with burst credit allocations (short-term burst allowances, e.g., 10–20% over committed capacity). Excludes reserved-contract negotiation and invoicing processes handled by Finance.

Definitions
- Burst credit: a short-term allowance enabling tenants to exceed committed throughput without immediate throttling.
- Adjudication: operator-led decision to adjust a tenant's credit balance or billing after investigation.
- Dispute ticket: a customer or automated alert requesting review of burst credit consumption.

Principles
1) Fast triage: most disputes are resolved within 4 business hours.
2) Observable decisions: every adjudication must include a justification, operator ID, query snapshot, and dashboard link.
3) Least privilege remediation: prefer non-billing fixes (rate limit changes, throttles, model variant swap) before credit adjustments.

Detection and Signal Sources
- Billing pipeline (scheduled job): nightly aggregation emits candidate anomalies where usage deviates > 200% of 7-day median for the tenant.
- Platform SLO alert: sustained token latency > 2x target or token-cost burn spikes tied to a single tenant tag.
- Customer Support: tickets labeled "burst-credit-dispute" from the support queue.
- Operator report: ad-hoc from oncall after investigating an incident.

Evidence Checklist for Triage
Operators must gather the following before making any adjustment: 
- 7-day and 30-day token consumption timeseries (UTC) for tenant.
- Per-model/route breakdown of tokens and peak qps.
- Recent deploys or feature flags affecting client behavior (timestamped).
- Recent model variant swaps or quantization rollouts.
- Network/region failover events that correlate with the window.
- Customer-provided request logs or replay samples (if available).

Automated Adjudication Rules (safe default)
- If anomaly duration < 10 minutes AND peak qps < 2x baseline: auto-close as transient; no credit action.
- If request pattern shows automated retry spike (>= 5 retries/minute from same client IP/tenant): recommend rate-limit change; do not credit.
- If anomaly coincides with rollback of client-side change flagged by Support: recommend credit equal to measured excess tokens above baseline, subject to manager approval.

Manual Adjudication Workflow (operator playbook)
1) Acknowledge ticket and set status to IN_TRIAGE in the operator portal. Add link to investigative dashboard.
2) Run the evidence collection queries (see Appendix SQL). Attach snapshots to ticket.
3) Attempt technical mitigations first (rate-limit, soft-throttle, immediate model swap, revert platform flag). Document change with timestamp and config diff.
4) If mitigation resolves and customer accepts operational remediation, close ticket with remediation summary.
5) If customer requests credit or evidence indicates system fault, escalate to the Billing Adjudication Queue. Include: measured excess tokens, justification (system fault / provider outage / unexpected fallback), and proposed credit amount.
6) Finance/billing performs final approval for credits > $5,000 (or equivalent token units).

Decision matrix (quick reference)
- Root cause: customer loop bug -> action: recommend client fix, deny credit, provide replay guidance.
- Root cause: platform regression (deploy/rollout) -> action: credit + rollback/mitigation, tag release, open postmortem.
- Root cause: third-party model backend failure -> action: partial credit, notify partners team.
- Root cause: one-off customer event (marketing campaign) -> action: offer goodwill credit at PM discretion (documented).

Dashboard and Alerting Recommendations
The following dashboard panels and alerts should be present in the Tenant Adjudication dashboard:
- Tenant consumption heatmap (24h / 7d / 30d) with hoverable percentile bands.
- Per-route token cost waterfall (last 24h): tokens by model variant, decoding length buckets, and request count.
- Retry storm detector: 1m and 5m windows, alerts when > 500 retries/min across tenant.
- Anomaly score panel: composite of rate deviation and cost-per-request delta. Alert threshold: score > 0.85
- Adjudication queue widget: tickets awaiting evidence, with SLA timers.

Suggested Alerts (examples):
- Burst-credit-anomaly-critical: triggered when tenant cost > 300% median and duration > 30 minutes. Pager to platform oncall.
- Burst-credit-notify: triggered when cost > 150% median for 3 consecutive hours. Email to customer success and support.

Runbook: Step-by-step (for platform oncall)
1) Receive alert or ticket. Verify tenant ID, window, and initial anomaly.
2) Open the Tenant Adjudication dashboard and filter by tenant id.
3) Capture screenshots and download CSV for the 1h, 6h, 24h windows.
4) Run the "replay-sample" script to capture 5 representative requests if logs are present.
5) If you identify automated client retries or obvious instrumentation bug, escalate to customer support and reference the client error signature.
6) Apply temporary traffic shaping (example CLI below) and measure impact for 10 minutes.
7) If the issue is platform-caused, tag the current serving commit and initiate a hotfix rollback per rollback runbook.
8) Complete adjudication form in ticket with evidence and recommended credit amount (if any). Close or escalate as appropriate.

Operator CLI and SQL snippets (examples)
- SQL: fetch 7-day median tokens
  SELECT tenant_id, date_trunc('hour', ts) as hour, sum(tokens) as tokens
  FROM token_usage
  WHERE tenant_id = 'TENANT_ID' AND ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
  GROUP BY 1,2
  ORDER BY hour;

- CLI: apply soft throttle (example)
  rdctl tenant throttle set --tenant TENANT_ID --qps 12 --duration 10m --reason "adjudication-temp-throttle"

Audit and Documentation Requirements
- Every adjudication must include at least: operator name, timestamp, data snapshots (7d/30d), action taken, ticket id, and if credit issued, the token amount and dollar equivalent.
- Store adjudication records in the "adjudications" table with immutable write-once fields (operator_id, timestamp, rationale, evidence_url).

Escalation Paths
- Billing Adjudication Queue (level 1): Finance + Platform lead — required for credits > $5000.
- Product/Security review (level 2): for suspected abuse or legal exposure.
- Leadership notification: for systemic regressions impacting >5% of tenants or multiregion incidents.

KPIs and SLOs for the Adjudication Process
- Mean time to triage: target <= 4 hours.
- Percent of disputes resolved without credit: target >= 65%.
- Audit completeness: 100% of adjudications contain evidence links and operator ID.

Rollout Plan and Backfill Strategy
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Deploy dashboard, automated anomaly job, and basic alerting (notify only). Train oncall with synthetic tickets.
- Phase 2 (1 month): Enable automated adjudication rules with opt-out. Monitor false positives for 2 weeks.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): Integrate with billing system for automatic small credits (< $200) and provide a monthly reconciliation report to Finance.

Appendix: Related pages and commands
- Related pages: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026, /confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-adjudication-criteria-2025
- Useful queries: sample token usage joins, replay scripts, and the rdctl helper reference (internal).

Change log
- 2025-03-12: Initial draft and operator checklist by Asha Kapoor.
- 2025-09-02: Added automated rules and dashboard panel names after pilot.
- 2026-01-18: Clarified escalation thresholds and added SQL/CLI snippets.
